audit_findings.title: Common-income numerator may contain cash-flow add-backs belonging to the 49.9% noncontrolling owner
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated depreciation and other OE add-backs, and potentially maintenance capex, may not be allocated consistently with the common-share net-income numerator.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2016, Black Hills Electric Generation sold a 49.9 %, non-controlling interest in Black Hills Colorado IPP to a third-party buyer.
audit_findings.explanation: The 49.9% noncontrolling ownership is demonstrated, and $8.2 million of 2025 NCI income was deducted from common income. The record does not demonstrate whether the OE add-backs were similarly reduced. Because subsidiary depreciation and maintenance capex are not supplied, neither the error nor its materiality is established.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct Black Hills Colorado IPP's annual D&A, other add-backs and maintenance capex, allocate 49.9% to NCI, and rerun the OE series and DCF if the existing bridge used consolidated amounts.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require future equity issuance absent from the static denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Future common issuance would increase the share denominator supporting projected OE growth; debt financing would instead reduce future OE through incremental interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: We plan to support and grow our business by using cash generated from operating activities and various financing alternatives, which could include our Revolving Credit Facility, our CP Program, and the issuance of common stock under our ATM program or in a secondary offering.
audit_findings.explanation: This is forward-looking rather than a demonstrated current error. The company issued 3.7 million shares in 2025 and 0.7 million during the first half of 2026, but the 76.984 million fully diluted denominator is current and therefore does not omit those historical issuances. The amount and timing of additional equity needed for the 4%-6% growth cases are not established.
audit_findings.action: Build annual capital sources-and-uses schedules for each growth case, including retained OE, debt and interest, customer contributions or advances, and new shares; rerun per-share values when financing plans become committed.

audit_findings.title: AFUDC may turn financed construction into apparent owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.6 million pre-tax in 2025 ($12.9 million AFUDC debt plus $10.7 million AFUDC equity), equal to 8.5% of the $278.1 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: AFUDC equity increases income and AFUDC debt reduces current interest expense, while the related growth construction capex is not deducted from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in the cost of regulated construction projects is AFUDC, when applicable, which represents the approximate composite cost of borrowed funds and a return on equity used to finance a regulated utility project.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed AFUDC amounts are demonstrated, but the supplied OE bridge does not establish whether they were removed; therefore the valuation error remains unresolved rather than proven. The disclosed 2025 amount is large relative to anchor OE and could materially move the valuation if retained and propagated through the forecast, especially because roughly half of scenario value comes from terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Trace AFUDC equity and capitalized interest through every historical OE year, remove their after-tax common-share effects where corresponding construction capex is excluded, and rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit claims may not be fully represented by periodic expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $130.4 million gross funded-status deficiency at December 31, 2025, or $1.69 per diluted share and 3.1% of $4,201 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrecoverable funding deficit belongs in the equity bridge, while cash contributions exceeding periodic expense would reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Supplemental Plans are subject to various vesting schedules and are funded on a cash basis as benefits are paid.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed deficiencies are $42.2 million for the pension plan, $47.4 million for supplemental plans and $40.8 million for healthcare. Even deducting the entire $130.4 million without credit for regulatory recovery would reduce base value from $54.57 to about $52.88 per share and bull value from $60.81 to about $59.12, still well below the $73.21 market price. Moreover, 2025 benefit contributions of $10.9 million did not exceed the $11.6 million periodic expense, so a current OE shortfall is not demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the portion recoverable through rates and deduct any nonrecoverable balance in the bridge; continue comparing annual cash contributions with OE expense, but no conclusion-changing rerun is indicated at the filed scale.

audit_findings.title: Finite-life production tax credits may have been capitalized as perpetual earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.3 million 2025 energy-related tax benefit, equal to 5.5% of the $278.1 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Unmodeled PTC expirations would lower future after-tax OE and the terminal earnings base; customer sharing may offset part of the effect.
audit_findings.evidence: This facility qualifies for PTCs at $30/MWh under IRC 45 during the 10-year period beginning on the date the facility was originally placed in service.
audit_findings.explanation: The ten-year credit lives and the 2025 tax benefit are demonstrated, while the valuation method provides no explicit expiration schedule. It is not established how much of the benefit entered the OE series: Peak View credits flow to customers, and ownership and sharing for the other facilities require tracing. A recurring amount equal to 5.5% of anchor OE, with facilities reaching the end of their credit periods around 2026-2030, is reasonably capable of materially changing forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Map 2025 credits by facility, ownership and customer-sharing treatment; normalize taxes as each credit expires and rerun the OE anchor, explicit forecast and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor input may contain a one-time captive-consolidation benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.5 million filed benefit; computed full-removal sensitivity is approximately $3.5 million, or 1.3%, of anchor OE and $0.68 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring benefit in 2025 OE affects the fitted historical log trend and therefore the forecast OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Consolidation of the Captive resulted in an increase in our net income o f $ 10.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $10.5 million benefit remained in OE is unresolved. However, because the model uses a ten-year log-trend anchor rather than 2025 actual OE, removing the full benefit from 2025 would reduce the fitted anchor from about $278.1 million to $274.6 million. Proportionally rerunning the operating PV would lower base value by about $0.68 per share, far short of the $18.64 gap between base value and the $73.21 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the captive true-up and the $9.9 million of 2025 merger costs through the OE bridge, apply the same normalization policy to both, and recompute the log-trend anchor; retain the finding as non-material unless tracing reveals additional affected years or amounts.
